_about.item: A8 test data: real-chess results of every king move in the engine suite (engine/suite/results.json), against the frozen-king convention's prediction that every king move loses.
_about.source: engine/suite/results.json (275 probed positions, Lichess 7-man tablebase); king-move results are the tablebase result for the MOVER. Flags 'immediate_stalemate' read offline from the cached Lichess records (engine/suite/tbcache, realchess/cache).
_about.headline_group: tame, race-insensitive, A-trebuchets: 94 positions, 449 king moves, 41 draw, 7 win (engine/suite/README.md, RESULTS.md section 1).
_about.groups: as in engine/suite/summarize.py: tame = no +-BIG in the CGT(count) value; race-sensitive = the CGT winning set depends on RACE_RULE; A_r trebuchet: W Pg r, B Pg r+1, WK f r+1, BK h r; B_r: same pawns, WK h r+1, BK f r.

fields.convention: the model's prediction for the king move: always 'loss' (it drops the mover's g-pawn).
fields.frozen_king_wrong: true iff at least one king move does not lose in real chess.
fields.king_move_changes_outcome: true iff the best king move is strictly better for the mover than the best pawn move, i.e. the frozen-king assumption alone makes the predicted outcome wrong.
fields.dist_to_nearest_enemy_component_pawn_*: Chebyshev distance from the king to the nearest enemy pawn on files a-d, before / after the move (derived from the FEN).
fields.convention_root_count_rule: 'win' iff CGT(count) predicts a winning pawn move; draws are never predicted.
